title: Arrow ends snap to anchor dots on shapes and re-anchor by dragging
body: Ends of a line or arrow attach to a shape by name with no side, so where they meet is hard to control. With the Line or Arrow tool, hovering a shape shows 9 dots (corners, side midpoints, centre); the pointer snaps to the nearest within a few screen pixels and an end dropped on one writes `NAME SIDE` or `NAME CORNER` (or the bare name for the centre). Elsewhere on the outline an end writes `NAME SIDE F`. A point inside a shape has no form in the language, so ends stay on the outline. A selected line or arrow shows a handle on each end; dragging it onto a dot or edge re-anchors that end, and dropping it on empty canvas detaches it to a point.
close_reason: Landed in 8a9536b. `anchor::anchor_at` and `Outline::dots` in `crates/acre-gui/src/anchor.rs` pick the spot. `tool::end_at` and `tool::end_edits` write it, and `Target::Line` in `handle.rs` gives a line its end handles. The library gained `scene::edit::end_edits`, `EndAt::On` and `Spot`. Inside a thing, away from its outline, an end writes the bare name. Row and matrix cells get no dots, and a merge's ends get no handles.
